about: The inventory registry for adamsville-play. The used-list is NOT kept here — tools/check_inventory.py DERIVES it from the code's own references on every run (Joshua's design amendment, 2026-10-17: a hand-kept roster decays). This file only DECLARES the legitimate non-referenced states: stock, tooling and doc files, by area, with reasons. A file that is neither referenced nor declared here is a true orphan and fails the gate. Tools that create stock add their declaration here as part of creating it.

declarations.reason: The shared stock shelf (ONE-SOURCE.md section 4): props, vocabularies and designs any editor — or the game — may use. Stock is present on purpose; no program has to reference it yet. Shelf layout is documented in editors/stock/README.md.

The Building Editor's pick-list vocabularies (floor-plan templates, fence styles, floor types, driveway materials, garage sides, house styles, decoration types, and the sibling lists in the same source block), copied verbatim out of the app's data.py onto the shared shelf 2026-10-17 (ONE-SOURCE.md section 4). These files are the canonical lists; the app still reads its baked-in copies until the Building Editor rebuild adopts the shelf.

Real CC0 surface textures (one 1024x1024 JPG colour map per material named in the Building Editor vocabularies), downloaded 2026-10-19 from Poly Haven and ambientCG — Joshua's Oct 11–12 order ('grab some free assets from the internet... brick, wood siding, vinyl siding, planks, brick') carried out for textures at last; the earlier free-assets run brought only the Kenney model kits. Provenance per file in editors/stock/textures/SOURCES.md. Resources only — no game code references them yet; wiring them into the renderer is a later step on Joshua's ruling.
UI Editor factory-default layout seed. The live stock is detailed/ui_layout.json; this is the reset-to-factory source, labelled as such.
Editor app sources, kept in the repo as the editors' source of record (each app's updater also downloads its own .py files from these paths).
Editor repo-side generator scripts (e.g. the Building Editor's index/live-status generators), run as part of editor save flows.
Editor web entry pages, part of the editor source sets.
Editor app icons (mollie-icon.png), part of the editor source sets.
Workflow copies kept with the editor sources from their old repos. Inert here — GitHub only runs workflows from the repo root .github/workflows.
Map Editor Blender workshop assets (world model, road objs). The placeable prop models moved to the shared shelf, editors/stock/props/.
Elevation Editor Blender workshop assets (parked editor, kept with its source set).

Detail Editor data (version.json). The Detail Editor (Joshua, 2026-10-18) is a live suite app; its updater reads version.json from this folder, and its app sources live under editors/detail-editor/app/.

Elevation Editor data (terrain.json, version.json). The Elevation Editor is parked by Joshua (2026-10-16) and its code still points at its pre-consolidation repo; these files are its data of record, kept with the source set until it is unparked.
Repo tooling (smoke test, CI check, this inventory checker).
Repo tooling (this inventory checker).
Repo tooling data (this registry).

Chess NPC source material: the prison score-sheet books (EPUB) that the chess NPC profiles are digitised from — the source of record for the cast of tools/generate-chess-npcs.js. Book 1 is final (annotated); book 2 joins it when its digitisation and opening-stamp pass finish.
The watcher app, source of record. Its game_sync.js loads the game's published files live; the other files are the app itself plus its offline fallbacks and reference photos.

Decision Deck queue generators (build-road-review-queue.py): they build deck queues out of the game's own zone data. The deck page itself is referenced code; the generators are the tooling that feeds it.

Decision Deck queue data files, generated from the game's zone data by the queue generators and loaded by the deck at runtime (the Adamsville road-review queue; the demo-meanings queue that proves gesture meanings come from queue data). Queue data is stock the deck reads — never baked into the deck's code.
Standalone map viewer apps (web / Android / Linux), source of record. They consume the game's published data; nothing in the game references them.
Map source data of record — the border-clipped OSM record the converted game map was built from (map-data/INVENTORY.md). Kept so research and rebuilds never start over.
Map source data of record (terrain tint for the map-data set).
Map source data of record (street names, terrain bands).
The converted map dataset of record (roads/buildings/water/terrain + its viewer), produced by the map conversion and read by its viewer and the diagnostics work.
Map diagnostics pages, served by Pages (road-buried-view.html and ground-compare-535.html are standing preview addresses). Instruments of the map toolchain.

The Google-Maps-style viewable map of the rebuilt world (Joshua, 2026-10-18): map-view.html (pan/zoom/search viewer with Street / Satellite (Esri World Imagery tiles) / Terrain base layers, aligned through the conversion's own lat/lon frame), its generated overview dataset map-view-overview.json, and the generator that rebuilds that dataset from the game's zone files. The viewer only READS map-data/ and detailed/zones/ — map-data is the read-only resource map, so the tool lives here, never inside it.
Research reference maps from the border/map research. Kept so the research is never redone.
Research reference map (the revised border). Kept so the research is never redone.
GitHub Pages config for the map-data subtree.
Live GitHub Actions workflows.
Repo config.
Folder marker. reports/ is the game's upload target (detailed/github_reports.js); the real files are created by the game at runtime, and git cannot hold an empty folder.
Folder marker. world-fixes/ is the world-fix sync folder (detailed/worldfix_sync.js); batch files are created by devices at runtime, and git cannot hold an empty folder.

Folder marker. drawings/ is the Draw for Mollie upload target (suite app: core/suite-draw.js + modules/draw-send.js); the real files (drawing PNGs and their sidecar notes) are created by the suite app at runtime, and git cannot hold an empty folder.

Generated snapshot of the 2026-10-17 clean-repo migration — the deriver's output at migration time (path, sha256, used-by/declaration for every file that moved). Regenerable by tools/check_inventory.py --snapshot; kept as the migration's record.
Project records and documentation (README, ONE-SOURCE.md, INVENTORY.md, dated work notes, editor READMEs, stock SOURCES notes).

Building Editor 2.0.0's derived detail chunks (rebuild spec: the snapshot model). Each zone's buildings_detail.json is split by editors/building-editor/generate_detail_chunks.py into per-cell chunk files the editor downloads on demand when a building is selected (the game's own detail files stay canonical; these are a generated access copy, regenerated by the editor's own saves for exactly the cells a save touched).

The shared suite core (Joshua's no-repeated-code law, 2026-10-17): the ONE Python library every editor consumes — GitHub round-trip with the 409-retry, the shared download cache, ground/lift math, the 3D viewport and building-snapshot renderers, the layout grammar, the About dialog, both updater halves, and Draw for Mollie. Consolidated 2026-10-18 into the suite_core package (EXTRACTION-REPORT.md section 4 executed); the top-level flat files are compatibility shims naming the package modules. Editors vendor snapshots of it at build time; this is its published home.

Runtime map packages for the multiple-maps system (Phase D, 2026-10-28): per-map data packages (zone/roads/buildings/water/rail/structures/places/pins/signs JSON + terrain.bin + the terrain-mesh precompute bin) loaded by detailed/map_loader.js from the registry's packageBase ('maps/<id>/' relative to detailed/). Package files are fetched by constructed path (base + filename), so no single literal reference names them — the same dataset status the zone files get from the zoneloader rule. Contents are authored data (the redrawn Adamsville package, Phase B), verified per-file by sha256 against the staging package at publish time.

Standalone 3D terrain preview pages (Joshua's Step-2 inspection slices, first: Dollar Mill / Utoy Circle to Boulder Park, 2026-10-28): a self-contained Three.js page rendering the USGS 3DEP terrain for one small area so Joshua can inspect the new ground — pan/zoom/orbit — before any of it becomes game map data. Preview only: nothing here is registered as game data.

Standalone 3D preview of the EXPANDED Step-2 terrain TEST package (Boulder Park Dr x Bakers Ferry to Fairburn Rd, MLK Jr Dr to Utoy Creek, 2026-10-28): renders the built package data itself (USGS 3DEP 10 m ground with carved waterways, measured lake levels, NLCD canopy masses) so Joshua can inspect it on phone and laptop before any of it becomes game map data. The game stays in its NO MAP DATA state; nothing here is registered as game data.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-28): two ranch houses on the Dollar Mill crest pad inside the terrain-test area, with individual trees derived from the package canopy data and a short Dollar Mill Rd stretch (7.2 m, no centre line) — built so Joshua can verify the clearing rule (no tree inside a house footprint + 6 m margin) and the intended look before the buildings step. Test scene only; renders from the test package without modifying it. The game stays in its NO MAP DATA state; nothing here is registered as game data.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-28): Tatum Lake with the crest scene's treatment (package terrain, real individual trees with the 8 ft foliage rule) plus its two features — the outlet falls as a boulder-step cascade (44 boulders; the audited 6.0 ft step broken into three ~2 ft drops, animated trickle + foam) and the Boulder Park Dr culvert (2.5 m diameter corrugated pipe, 19 m, road at grade over the fill, mouths open on both faces) — and the canopy-off-open-water rule applied to its trees (0 of 478 in the lake or any open water). Built so Joshua can verify the falls/culvert treatments before the water/structures step. Test scene only; renders from the test package without modifying it. The game stays in its NO MAP DATA state; nothing here is registered as game data.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-29): the I-20 x Fairburn Rd overpass with the crest/Tatum treatment (package terrain, 715 real individual trees with the 8 ft foliage rule). Fairburn passes OVER I-20 on a 70 m clear-span deck (slab + 5 girders + parapets, 4.92 m / 16.1 ft clearance) built TO the audited ground: the package terrain under the span is the freeway's natural bench (263.4 m at the crossing (33.76595, -84.50012), falling 275.9 m west to 261.8 m east; scene levelling under the span at most 0.80 m, raised at most 0.11 m), fill only at the abutment approaches (max 3.29 m). Records that the archived road centrelines near this crossing are internally inconsistent (freeway lines bunched/duplicated), so the scene seats the freeway in the DEM bench. Test scene only; renders from the test package without modifying it. The game stays in its NO MAP DATA state.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-29): the at-grade railroad crossing on Boulder Park Dr SW — CSX Atlanta Terminal Subdivision (redraw record AN-05-001) at (33.74983, -84.50144), ~440 m east of Fairburn Rd — with the same treatment as the crest/Tatum scenes (terrain-test package terrain, real individual trees with the 8 ft foliage rule) plus the rail-grade doctrine made visible: the line holds an engineered near-level grade (scene grade anchored to the record profile at the crossing, 877.5 ft, 1.6% ruling south), the terrain is cut (to -3.23 m SSE) and filled (to +1.24 m NNW) to meet it, Boulder Park Dr's profile flattens onto the rail-top level, rails and ties run continuous through a crossing panel, crossbuck + flashing-light signals on both approaches. Clearings verified: 0 of 570 trees in the road corridor, 0 in the rail corridor, 0 in open water. The record profile's ~4% dive SSE of the crossing is flagged in the scene audit for the rail-authoring step. Test scene only; renders from the test package without modifying it. The game stays in its NO MAP DATA state; nothing here is registered as game data.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-29): the MLK (GA-139) x I-285 interchange, exit 9 — the third crossing type, built so Joshua can compare it against the plain overpass: MLK passes OVER I-285 on an 80 m deck at 886 ft (clearance 5.11 m / 16.8 ft over the freeway's 862 ft surface), and ONE ramp pair carries the terrain story — the SE loop off-ramp climbs from I-285's level to MLK on rising earthworks and the SW on-ramp descends back (redraw package ramp geometries and their recorded profiles, smoothed fitted centrelines throughout). The crossing sits ~390 m east of the terrain-test package, so the ground is an EXTENSION built from the same USGS 3DEP tile by the same method on the same frame lattice (declared in the scene); 2,266 real individual trees (8 ft foliage rule, NLCD canopy with its east edge extended by nearest column, also declared). Standing-gate audits on the delivered build: coverage/flanking — zero covered points on every drawn surface (111k+ samples, deck air check clean); ribbon quality — all surfaces from smoothed fitted centrelines at <=2.1 m stations, centreline sawtooth <=0.060 m, constant width exact. Test scene only; the game stays in its NO MAP DATA state.

Standalone 3D look-test (Step 2, 2026-10-29): the WHOLE Adamsville zone's Stage-1 terrain foundation — pure ground at Joshua's ruled D mix (2 m near roads/houses, 10 m elsewhere; preview mesh decimated for the web to 8 m near / 30 m far, heights sampled from the stage-1 package grids only, reconstruction verified exact at all 11,032,992 near posts). Heights are the USGS 1 m lidar truth (100% coverage); 23 surveyed water bodies drawn at their levels, 54 pending-bed basins as outlines only (no invented water); no roads, houses or carved channels (stage 2 awaits rulings). Test scene only; the game stays in its NO MAP DATA state.
